chapter_summary: A thin glimmer catches the eye and threatens to hide the rough work beneath it. She leaves part of the edge unresolved so the image cannot pretend to be seamless.

spatality.place: a panel's edge where gold leaf meets unfinished plaster
spatality.season: night, the last hour before lamplight is useless
spatality.route: from the gilded edge inward to the working surface
spatality.texture: thin gold catching the flame, rough plaster beside it, the smell of size

poetic_parameters.movement: New Formalism — formal constraint as conscience, here the discipline of leaving an edge unfinished.
writing_skills: ceremonial cadence built on a single repeated image
antithesis of gold and rough plaster
a close that chooses incompleteness over display
poetic_parameters.image_seed: a strip of gold leaf stopping abruptly where the plaster has not been smoothed
poetic_parameters.volta: from admiring the gold as the poem's climax to leaving the edge deliberately dull
poetic_parameters.sonic_texture: the bright ring of gold, leaf, edge cut against the flat u of rough
poetic_parameters.line_gesture: ceremonial, slightly formal lines that break once, hard, at the unfinished edge
poetic_parameters.variety_note: Chapter twenty-one refused to beautify anonymity; this poem refuses to beautify completion, and is the book's most deliberately formal piece.
poetic_parameters.metaphor_family: gilding, seam, and the seam left visible
poetic_parameters.address: the gold leaf, then the self as its steward
poetic_parameters.closing_move: the unfinished edge named as the poem's own truth-telling
